title: Can, could, may
point: Use can for ability and casual requests, could for softer requests or past ability, and may for formal permission.

sentences.ja: 私、全然泳げないんだよね。
sentences.text: I can't swim at all, actually.
Can you pass me the salt?
sentences.note: Between friends, "Can you...?" is a request, not a question about ability.

sentences.ja: もう少しゆっくり話していただけますか？
sentences.text: Could you speak a little more slowly?

sentences.ja: ちょっと質問してもよろしいでしょうか？
sentences.text: May I ask you a quick question?

sentences.ja: 子どもの頃は逆立ちができたんだ。
sentences.text: I could do a handstand when I was a kid.

sentences.ja: ごめん、今聞こえなかった。音声が途切れたみたい。
sentences.text: Sorry, I couldn't hear you. You cut out for a second.
sentences.note: "Cut out" is what people say when the sound drops on a call.

sentences.ja: ここに荷物置いてもいい？
sentences.text: Can I leave my bag here for a minute?

sentences.ja: 今日の会議の資料、メールで送っていただけますか？
sentences.text: Could you email me the materials from today's meeting?
sentences.note: "Email" works as a verb, and 資料 is usually "materials" or "documents".

sentences.ja: 図書館では本を一度に五冊まで借りられます。
sentences.text: You can borrow up to five books at a time from the library.

sentences.ja: 金曜までに課題を終わらせられるかわからない。
sentences.text: I'm not sure I can finish the assignment by Friday.
sentences.note: "I'm not sure" plus a clause sounds more natural than "I don't know if" here.
